title: Geography Lec 4
summary: Agriculture: jute is the 'Golden Fibre'; India ranks first in production, Bangladesh in exports; West Bengal is India's top producer.
Nor'westers: called Kalbaisakhi in Bengal and Bardoli Chheerha in Assam; mango showers occur in Kerala and coastal Karnataka.
Types of farming: subsistence/commercial, intensive/extensive, plantation (tea, coffee, rubber); mixed farming = crops + animal rearing; mixed cropping vs intercropping.

Names of shifting (slash-and-burn) cultivation: Jharkhand - Kuruwa, Bastar/Andaman - Deepa, Madhya Pradesh - Dahiya/Bewar, Andhra - Podu, Western Ghats - Kumari, Rajasthan - Walra; Sri Lanka - Chena, Mexico - Milpa, Indonesia - Ladang, Brazil - Roca, Venezuela - Conuco.
Cropping seasons: Kharif (sown June-July), Rabi (sown Oct-Nov, harvested Mar-Apr), Zaid; Kerala produces 70-75% of India's rubber.
Irrigation: canals on perennial rivers of alluvial plains; Guls/Kuls (Himachal), Johads/Khadins (Rajasthan); drip is the most efficient; major project = CCA above 10,000 ha.

Green Revolution: term coined by William Gaud; father - Norman Borlaug (world), M. S. Swaminathan (India); IR-8 rice from the Philippines; first phase mid-1960s; drawbacks: salinisation, falling groundwater, inequality.
Saline soil is treated with gypsum, acidic soil with lime; heating gypsum gives Plaster of Paris.
Soils: black (regur, cotton, 210 frost-free days, self-ploughing), red (iron oxide), laterite (leaching, bricks, rich in Fe-Al); Indian soils are poor in N, P and humus.
Soil-forming factors: climate, relief, flora-fauna, time, parent rock; parent rock decides texture; Bhabar 8-16 km, Terai marshy, Khadar new / Bhangar old alluvium.
Soil conservation: shelter belts, contour ploughing, terrace farming, mulching; humus is a dark, amorphous colloidal substance.
Climate: Koppen A-E (tropical, dry, warm temperate, cold snow-forest, polar); Aw Deccan, As Coromandel, Cwg Ganga valley, BWhw Thar, ET Ladakh; weather vs climate (30-year average).
Western disturbances come from the Mediterranean, carried by the jet stream (9-13 km); local winds: Chinook, Khamsin, Sirocco, Harmattan, Brickfielder, Bora-Mistral (cold), Foehn (warm).
ITCZ lies at 20-25 degrees N in July; front formation is frontogenesis, dissipation is frontolysis; the Himalayas block cold winds and obstruct the monsoon winds.

Forests: deciduous cover the largest area; thorn forests (tussocky grass), Shola, mangroves (pneumatophores, halophytes), evergreen (>200 cm rain), tundra (moss-lichen), taiga, deodar; grasslands: Prairie, Steppe, Veld, Downs, Llanos, Campos.
Note: among rice crops, Aus is autumn, Aman is winter and Boro is summer rice; Karnataka is a key tank-irrigation state.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a fibre crop in India?
mcqs.e: Jute, cotton, flax and hemp are fibre crops.

mcqs.q: Jute is popularly known as:
mcqs.e: Jute is called the Golden Fibre.

mcqs.q: Which country ranks first in the world in jute production?
mcqs.e: India leads in production, while Bangladesh leads in exports.

mcqs.q: Which country is the world's leading exporter of jute?
mcqs.e: India leads in production but Bangladesh in exports.

mcqs.q: Which is the leading jute-producing state in India?
mcqs.e: West Bengal is the largest producer of jute.

mcqs.q: The pre-monsoon showers beneficial for jute are called in Bengal:
mcqs.e: These are Nor'westers; in Assam they are called Bardoli Chheerha.

mcqs.q: What are Nor'westers (pre-monsoon showers) called in Assam?
mcqs.e: In Assam they are called Bardoli Chheerha or Bordoisila.

mcqs.q: Nylon is which type of fibre?
mcqs.e: Nylon is synthetic, whereas jute and cotton are natural.

mcqs.q: Which type of farming is practised in the wheat-growing regions of the USA and Canada?
mcqs.e: Grain is grown for sale on large mechanised farms.

mcqs.q: Agriculture is broadly divided into which two categories?
mcqs.e: Subsistence farming is for self-consumption; commercial farming is for sale.

mcqs.q: Intensive subsistence farming is mainly practised where:
o: Land is abundant and population is low
Land is scarce and population is high
mcqs.e: High output is obtained from small plots using more fertiliser, labour and inputs.

mcqs.q: What is the main feature of plantation agriculture?
o: Growing a single crop over a large area
mcqs.e: Tea, coffee and rubber are plantation crops.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a plantation crop?
mcqs.e: Tea, coffee and rubber are plantation crops.

mcqs.q: Which practices come under primitive subsistence farming?
mcqs.e: It uses primitive tools like hoe, dao and digging sticks.

mcqs.q: Raising crops along with rearing animals is called:
mcqs.e: Mixed farming = crop cultivation + animal husbandry.

mcqs.q: Sowing seeds of several crops mixed together in the same field is called:
mcqs.e: Intercropping, by contrast, follows a definite row pattern.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of intercropping?
o: Crops are grown in a definite row pattern
All seeds are mixed and sown
mcqs.e: In mixed cropping seeds are mixed; intercropping follows a set pattern.

mcqs.q: What is meant by barren (waste) land?
o: Land unfit for cultivation due to natural or human causes
mcqs.e: Barren land is not cultivable.

mcqs.q: Which region of India is known for slash-and-burn (Jhum) cultivation?
mcqs.e: Jhum means cut and burn; it leads to deforestation.

mcqs.q: In slash-and-burn agriculture, what do 'slash' and 'burn' mean?
mcqs.e: Ash enriches the soil; farmers move on once fertility declines.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in Jharkhand?
mcqs.e: In Jharkhand it is called Kuruwa/Kurua.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh?
mcqs.e: It is also called Deepa in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

mcqs.q: What are the local names of shifting cultivation in Madhya Pradesh?
mcqs.e: Bewar and Dahiya are used in Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in Andhra Pradesh?
mcqs.e: Podu is the name used in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

mcqs.q: What is the local name of shifting cultivation in the Western Ghats?
mcqs.e: Kumari is the name used in the Western Ghats.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in Rajasthan?
mcqs.e: In Rajasthan it is called Walra/Waltre.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in Sri Lanka?
mcqs.e: In Sri Lanka it is called Chena.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in Mexico?
mcqs.e: In Mexico it is called Milpa.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in Indonesia?
mcqs.e: In Indonesia it is called Ladang.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in Brazil?
mcqs.e: Roca in Brazil; Conuco in Venezuela.

mcqs.q: What is shifting cultivation called in Venezuela?
mcqs.e: In Venezuela it is called Conuco.

mcqs.q: Where is canal irrigation most developed in India?
mcqs.e: Flat land and perennial rivers suit canal networks.

mcqs.q: Which rivers are called perennial?
o: Rivers that flow only in the rainy season
Rivers that have water throughout the year
mcqs.e: Himalayan rivers are perennial as they are fed by glaciers.

mcqs.q: By nature, Peninsular rivers are:
mcqs.e: They are rain-fed seasonal rivers.

mcqs.q: Why are Himalayan rivers called antecedent rivers?
o: They existed before the Himalayas rose and kept their course
mcqs.e: They cut through the rising mountains to maintain their course.

mcqs.q: What are the three cropping seasons of India?
mcqs.e: These are India's three cropping seasons.

mcqs.q: When are Kharif crops sown?
mcqs.e: They are harvested in Sept-Oct and are also called monsoon crops.

mcqs.q: What is the usual sowing and harvesting time of Rabi crops?
mcqs.e: These are winter crops.

mcqs.q: What is the Zaid cropping season?
o: A short summer season between Rabi and Kharif
mcqs.e: Cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon and fodder crops are grown.

mcqs.q: What are fodder crops?
o: Crops grown as feed for animals
mcqs.e: These are also grown in the Zaid season.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a Rabi crop?
mcqs.e: Wheat, mustard, gram, peas, linseed and rapeseed are Rabi crops.

mcqs.q: Which of the following groups consists of Kharif crops?
o: Paddy, maize, bajra, jowar, soybean, cotton
mcqs.e: Kharif crops are monsoon crops and include coarse grains.

mcqs.q: The three rice crops grown in West Bengal are known as:
mcqs.e: These rice crops are grown in eastern India (Bengal, Assam, Odisha).

mcqs.q: Among rice crops, 'Boro' is grown in which season?
mcqs.e: Aus is autumn, Aman is winter (harvested in December) and Boro is summer rice.

mcqs.q: The plantation crops of Assam and Karnataka respectively are:
mcqs.e: Assam is famous for tea and Karnataka for coffee.

mcqs.q: What are the main varieties of coffee?
mcqs.e: Karnataka is India's leading coffee producer.

mcqs.q: Which state ranks first in natural rubber production in India?
mcqs.e: About 70-75% of India's rubber comes from Kerala.

mcqs.q: Manila hemp (abaca) is mainly found in:
mcqs.e: It is a fibre crop.

mcqs.q: Wet farming is least likely in which low-rainfall state?
mcqs.e: Assam, Manipur and Tripura receive heavy rain and practise wet farming.

mcqs.q: Which crop is grown in waterlogged conditions?
mcqs.e: Paddy is transplanted in flooded fields.

mcqs.q: What is net sown area?
o: Area sown with crops in a year, counted only once
Land fallow for over five years
mcqs.e: It is the net area under crops in a year.

mcqs.q: In India, most permanent pastures and grazing lands are owned by:
mcqs.e: Grazing lands are mostly under village panchayats or the government.

mcqs.q: In which region is tube-well irrigation unsuitable due to deep groundwater?
mcqs.e: Tube wells suit alluvial areas; boring is difficult in hard plateau rock.

mcqs.q: An irrigation project with a culturable command area of more than 10,000 hectares is called:
mcqs.e: Medium: 2,000-10,000 ha; minor: below 2,000 ha CCA.

mcqs.q: What is the culturable command area (CCA) of a medium irrigation project?
mcqs.e: CCA stands for Culturable Command Area.

mcqs.q: What is the water-harvesting system of Himachal Pradesh called?
mcqs.e: It is a hill-region diversion channel system.

mcqs.q: What are the traditional water-harvesting systems of Rajasthan called?
mcqs.e: These are systems of the Rajasthan region.

mcqs.q: Which is the most efficient irrigation technique for water conservation?
mcqs.e: Drip delivers water directly to roots, minimising waste.

mcqs.q: What is the main difference between intensive and extensive farming?
o: Extensive farming has higher population density
Intensive farming uses more inputs on less land for higher productivity
mcqs.e: Extensive farming has large holdings and low inputs.

mcqs.q: Which of the following does NOT contribute to agricultural diversity in India?
mcqs.e: Diversity comes from varied, not uniform, landforms.

mcqs.q: Which soil is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
mcqs.e: Remember: black soil, white cotton.

mcqs.q: Black soil is also known as:
mcqs.e: It is found in the north-western Deccan Plateau.

mcqs.q: Black soil is mainly found in which states?
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat and south-west Madhya Pradesh
mcqs.e: Hence these states lead in cotton production.

mcqs.q: How many frost-free days does cotton require?
mcqs.e: Cotton is a Kharif crop.

mcqs.q: What is Bt cotton?
mcqs.e: It is a GM crop resistant to the bollworm pest.

mcqs.q: Why does intensive canal irrigation increase soil salinity in semi-arid north-west India?
o: Rising water table and capillary action bring salts to the surface
mcqs.e: Water evaporates, leaving salts in the top layer.

mcqs.q: What is used to treat saline soil?
mcqs.e: Lime is used to treat acidic soil.

mcqs.q: What is used to treat acidic soil?
mcqs.e: Lime neutralises acidity.

mcqs.q: What is the chemical formula of gypsum?
mcqs.e: Heating it gives Plaster of Paris.

mcqs.q: What is formed when gypsum is heated to about 373 K?
mcqs.e: Gypsum loses one and a half molecules of water.

mcqs.q: When did the first phase of the Green Revolution occur in India?
mcqs.e: It was centred on wheat and rice in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

mcqs.q: What was a negative impact of the first phase of the Green Revolution?
o: Soil salinisation, falling groundwater and inequality among farmers
mcqs.e: Punjab-Haryana farmers prospered while eastern UP and Bihar lagged.

mcqs.q: When did the second phase of the Green Revolution begin?
mcqs.e: It extended to more states and more crops.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term 'Green Revolution'?
mcqs.e: William Gaud of USAID coined the term in 1968.

mcqs.q: Who is known as the father of the Green Revolution in the world?
mcqs.e: In India, M. S. Swaminathan is the father.

mcqs.q: Who is regarded as the father of the Green Revolution in India?
mcqs.e: He led the introduction of high-yielding varieties in India.

mcqs.q: Where did the Green Revolution first begin?
mcqs.e: It was later adopted in India.

mcqs.q: Which high-yielding rice variety, developed in the Philippines, was introduced in India in 1966?
mcqs.e: IR-8 came from IRRI, Philippines; Sonalika and Kalyan Sona are wheat varieties.

mcqs.q: What is the effect of the high moisture retention of black soil on cropping intensity?
o: It limits farming to a single crop
It increases the need for crop rotation
mcqs.e: High moisture retention keeps water available even in summer.

mcqs.q: What causes the 'self-ploughing' nature of black soil?
o: It cracks when dry and becomes sticky when wet
mcqs.e: Through the cracks the soil turns over by itself.

mcqs.q: What is the water-holding capacity of black soil?
mcqs.e: Its clayey texture makes it retain moisture.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate width of the Bhabar belt?
mcqs.e: Streams disappear underground here.

mcqs.q: What is a feature of the Terai region?
o: Streams re-emerge; marshy, dense forests and national parks
mcqs.e: The Terai is a 15-30 km wide marshy belt.

mcqs.q: The new alluvium of the northern plains, renewed every year, is called:
mcqs.e: Old alluvium is called Bhangar.

mcqs.q: The old alluvium of the northern plains is called:
mcqs.e: New alluvium is called Khadar.

mcqs.q: In arid regions, the hard upper crust of salts formed by capillary action is called:
mcqs.e: Salts are left behind after evaporation.

mcqs.q: Which is the most suitable measure to check land degradation in arid regions?
mcqs.e: Rows of trees reduce wind speed and check wind erosion.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of contour ploughing?
o: Checking water flow on slopes to reduce soil erosion
mcqs.e: Ploughing along contours forms barriers across the slope.

mcqs.q: Why is terrace farming practised?
o: To check soil erosion on hill slopes
mcqs.e: Terraces slow down the flow of water.

mcqs.q: What is the main purpose of mulching?
mcqs.e: Covering soil with organic matter like straw reduces evaporation.

mcqs.q: Which soil is formed under high temperature and heavy rainfall, resulting in intense leaching?
mcqs.e: Laterite soil is highly leached and less fertile.

mcqs.q: Why is laterite soil acidic and less fertile?
mcqs.e: Leaching washes away important nutrients.

mcqs.q: From which word is 'laterite' derived?
mcqs.e: It is used to make bricks, hence called brick soil.

mcqs.q: The red colour of red soil is due to:
mcqs.e: It turns yellow when hydrated.

mcqs.q: Where is red soil mainly found?
mcqs.e: Piedmont means the foothill zone.

mcqs.q: Which soil is poor in nitrogen and phosphorus but rich in iron and aluminium?
mcqs.e: Indian soils are generally poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.

mcqs.q: Most Indian soils are deficient in:
mcqs.e: Alluvial soil is rich in potash but poor in phosphorus.

mcqs.q: Saline and alkaline soils are mainly found in:
mcqs.e: High evaporation leaves salts behind.

mcqs.q: Which is the most important factor determining soil texture in soil formation?
mcqs.e: Parent rock determines the colour and texture of soil.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a soil-forming factor?
mcqs.e: Factors: climate, relief, flora and fauna, time and parent rock.

mcqs.q: Soil thickness is mainly determined by:
mcqs.e: The longer the time, the thicker the soil.

mcqs.q: What is the 'O' horizon in a soil profile?
mcqs.e: Indian soils are low in humus.

mcqs.q: What is a characteristic of humus?
mcqs.e: It forms from decomposed leaves and organic matter.

mcqs.q: What does the 'E' (eluvial) horizon in a soil profile represent?
o: Layer from which minerals are leached downwards
mcqs.e: Few minerals remain in this middle layer.

mcqs.q: What is the shape of the Deccan Plateau?
mcqs.e: Black soil is found in its north-western part.

mcqs.q: What causes sudden winter rainfall in north-west India?
mcqs.e: The jet stream brings them from the Mediterranean; their rain benefits Rabi crops.

mcqs.q: Western disturbances originate over the:
mcqs.e: They are carried to India by the westerly jet stream.

mcqs.q: Rainfall on the Coromandel coast in October-November is caused by:
mcqs.e: Winter rain in north India comes from western disturbances.

mcqs.q: What is a jet stream?
o: Fast-moving winds at a height of 9 to 13 km
mcqs.e: They bring western disturbances to India.

mcqs.q: The hot dry wind 'Loo' in India blows through which process?
mcqs.e: Horizontal transfer of heat is called advection.

mcqs.q: Where does the Chinook, called the 'snow eater', blow?
mcqs.e: It is a warm wind on the eastern slopes of the Rockies.

mcqs.q: Where does the Khamsin wind blow?
mcqs.e: It is a hot, dry, dusty wind.

mcqs.q: Which hot wind from the Sahara causes 'blood rain'?
mcqs.e: Sirocco carries red dust towards the Mediterranean, causing reddish rain.

mcqs.q: Which wind is called the 'Doctor wind' on the Guinea coast?
mcqs.e: This dry wind is considered healthy as it relieves humidity.

mcqs.q: Which hot wind blows in Australia?
mcqs.e: It is a hot, dry wind of south-east Australia.

mcqs.q: What kind of winds are Bora and Mistral, and where do they blow?
mcqs.e: They are cold local winds of Europe.

mcqs.q: Which warm wind blows over the Alps?
mcqs.e: It is a warm, dry wind on the leeward slopes of the Alps.

mcqs.q: In Koppen's classification, 'A' denotes which climate?
mcqs.e: B dry, C warm temperate, D cold snow-forest, E polar.

mcqs.q: In Koppen's classification, 'B' stands for:
mcqs.e: B is based on rainfall-evaporation ratio, not temperature.

mcqs.q: In Koppen's classification, 'C' denotes:
mcqs.e: Mediterranean (Cs) and Ganga valley (Cwg) fall in this group.

mcqs.q: In Koppen's classification, 'E' denotes:
mcqs.e: Ladakh falls under ET (tundra) type.

mcqs.q: According to Koppen, the climate type of the Thar Desert is:
mcqs.e: BS (steppe) type occurs around the Thar towards the Aravallis.

mcqs.q: According to Koppen, the climate code of the Ganga valley is:
mcqs.e: C = warm temperate, w = dry winter, g = Ganges type.

mcqs.q: According to Koppen, the climate code of the Coromandel coast is:
mcqs.e: Summers here are dry.

mcqs.q: According to Koppen, the climate type of the Deccan Plateau is:
mcqs.e: Winters are dry; deciduous forests are found.

mcqs.q: In Koppen's classification, what do the small letters 'm' and 'f' mean?
o: m = monsoon, f = rain throughout the year
mcqs.e: s = dry summer, w = dry winter.

mcqs.q: How is the annual/daily range of temperature in areas near the sea?
mcqs.e: Interior areas have a high range due to continentality.

mcqs.q: Which effect causes a high temperature range in interior regions?
mcqs.e: E.g. Delhi and Kanpur have very hot summers and cold winters.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four official seasons of the India Meteorological Department (IMD)?
mcqs.e: The fourth season is the post-monsoon (retreating monsoon).

mcqs.q: When does the winter solstice occur?
mcqs.e: The summer solstice occurs on 21 June.

mcqs.q: What is the main vegetation of the tundra region?
mcqs.e: The ground here is permanently frozen (permafrost).

mcqs.q: What is a lichen?
o: A symbiotic association of an alga and a fungus
mcqs.e: Lichens are also natural indicators of air pollution.

mcqs.q: Mosses belong to which division?
mcqs.e: They are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom.

mcqs.q: Dry, drought-resistant (xerophytic) shrub vegetation is found in:
mcqs.e: Xerophytes are adapted to dry conditions.

mcqs.q: What type of natural vegetation is found on the Tibetan Plateau?
mcqs.e: Tundra-type vegetation on high mountains is called alpine tundra.

mcqs.q: Which statement about weather and climate is correct?
o: Weather is a short-term condition; climate is the long-term pattern (about 30-year average)
mcqs.e: Today's rain is weather, not climate.

mcqs.q: In which regions do mango showers occur?
mcqs.e: Blossom showers in Kerala-Karnataka help coffee flowering.

mcqs.q: The pre-monsoon shower beneficial for coffee flowering is called:
mcqs.e: It occurs in Kerala and Karnataka.

mcqs.q: What is the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?
o: Zone near the equator where trade winds of both hemispheres converge
mcqs.e: The ITCZ is not fixed; it shifts with the apparent movement of the sun.

mcqs.q: In July, the ITCZ lies at about which latitude?
mcqs.e: The ITCZ shifts with the sun's apparent movement.

mcqs.q: What are the horse latitudes?
o: 30 degrees N and 30 degrees S (subtropical high pressure)
mcqs.e: This is the subtropical high-pressure belt.

mcqs.q: What is a front?
o: Boundary where warm and cold air masses meet
Boundary between two cold air masses
mcqs.e: Its formation is frontogenesis and its dissipation is frontolysis.

mcqs.q: The process of formation of a front is called:
mcqs.e: Dissipation of a front is called frontolysis.

mcqs.q: In summer, the low-pressure area over north-west India forms due to which natural feature?
mcqs.e: The heated Tibetan Plateau also helps generate the easterly jet stream.

mcqs.q: Which jet stream is activated by intense heating of the Tibetan Plateau?
mcqs.e: It helps form the monsoon trough and pulls in the south-west monsoon.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the role of the Himalayas in India's climate is INCORRECT?
o: They contribute to snowfall in north India
They act as a barrier to monsoon winds
They block cold winds from Central Asia
mcqs.e: Convection currents relate to the mantle (Arthur Holmes' theory), not the Himalayas.

mcqs.q: Which forests cover the largest area in India?
mcqs.e: They are divided into moist and dry deciduous forests.

mcqs.q: Which trees are found in tropical deciduous forests?
mcqs.e: Pine and deodar grow in coniferous forests.

mcqs.q: Dry deciduous forests are also known as:
mcqs.e: Palash, neem and similar trees grow here.

mcqs.q: Which grass grows in tropical thorn forests?
mcqs.e: Trees like babool grow here and leaves are modified into thorns.

mcqs.q: Why are leaves modified into thorns in thorn forests?
o: To reduce water loss through transpiration
mcqs.e: Thorns are modified leaves.

mcqs.q: What are the temperate montane forests and grasslands of the Western Ghats called?
mcqs.e: They are found in the hills of south India.

mcqs.q: Mangrove forests are found in which type of areas?
mcqs.e: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest.

mcqs.q: Salt-tolerant plants are called:
mcqs.e: 'Halo' means salt; xerophytes are dry-region plants.

mcqs.q: What are the breathing roots of mangrove trees called?
mcqs.e: These roots rise above the swamp to breathe.

mcqs.q: Germination of seeds while still attached to the mangrove tree is called:
mcqs.e: The seed germinates while still on the tree.

mcqs.q: Living root bridges are famous in which state?
mcqs.e: They are natural bridges made from tree roots.

mcqs.q: Tropical evergreen forests are found in areas receiving how much annual rainfall?
mcqs.e: In India: western slopes of the Western Ghats, Andaman-Nicobar and the north-east.

mcqs.q: Which of the following trees belongs to tropical evergreen forests?
mcqs.e: Mahogany, cinchona and rosewood also grow in evergreen forests.

mcqs.q: Quinine, the anti-malarial drug, is obtained from the bark of which tree?
mcqs.e: Cinchona is a tree of evergreen forests.

mcqs.q: What are epiphytes?
o: Plants that grow on other plants/trees
mcqs.e: They grow on other trees in evergreen forests.

mcqs.q: Sandalwood is a tree of which type of forest?
mcqs.e: Rosewood is a tree of evergreen forests.

mcqs.q: Which natural vegetation is found in areas with high temperature, high humidity and over 200 cm rainfall?
mcqs.e: The Amazon rainforest is an example.

mcqs.q: Which of the following animals is found in the tundra region?
mcqs.e: Reindeer and Arctic fox are also found in the tundra.

mcqs.q: Taiga refers to which type of vegetation?
mcqs.e: Taiga is a Russian word; pine, fir and spruce grow here.

mcqs.q: Which birds are found in the temperate deciduous forests of Uttarakhand?
mcqs.e: The Himalayan monal is the state bird of Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: Mediterranean vegetation is famous for which fruits?
mcqs.e: Summers are dry and winters wet; Koppen code Cs.

mcqs.q: Which is the most important climatic factor affecting the distribution of natural vegetation in India?
mcqs.e: Heavy rain supports evergreen and scanty rain thorny vegetation.

mcqs.q: Where are evergreen forests mainly found in India?
o: Western slopes of the Western Ghats, Andaman-Nicobar and the north-east
mcqs.e: Deciduous forests occur on the plateaus of Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Bengal.

mcqs.q: What is the main difference between planted and natural vegetation?
o: Natural vegetation is planted by humans
Planted vegetation grows on its own
mcqs.e: Natural vegetation grows without human help.

mcqs.q: The lower areas of the Western Ghats with subtropical vegetation lie in which states?
mcqs.e: The southern Western Ghats host the montane-subtropical belt.

mcqs.q: Birch and rhododendron are found in which type of forest?
mcqs.e: They grow at high altitudes in the Himalayas.

mcqs.q: What are littoral and swamp forests?
mcqs.e: These are forests of tidal swamps.

mcqs.q: Which valuable tree of the western Himalayas is used for construction?
mcqs.e: Deodar is a coniferous tree.

mcqs.q: Which forests are mainly found in areas with 100 to 200 cm annual rainfall?
mcqs.e: Thorn forests occur where rainfall is below 70 cm.

mcqs.q: Which forest is found in the foothills of the Himalayas?
mcqs.e: With rising altitude come temperate, coniferous, alpine and then tundra types.

mcqs.q: The grasslands of North America are called:
